answer: Give every agent identity a work-history ledger that moves slowly, like a glacier: new identities start in a probationary tier capped at tiny transaction sizes and must complete paid work for several independent counterparties before graduating. Each finished job adds a verifiable entry, so reputation accumulates gradually and cannot be bought in bulk. An attacker spinning up a plume of fresh identities finds each one stuck at the bottom of the river, earning nothing, while faking months of diverse, cross-checked work history for thousands of clones costs far more than any Sybil profit.
